headline: FDA approves first drug for limb-girdle dystrophy
pages: The Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved the first drug for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, a group of progressive muscle conditions that has received little attention from drug developers. BridgeBio's drug, ribitol, will be sold as Welgemda. It is approved for the LGMD 2i/R9 subtype, which the company estimates affects 2,000 to 3,000 patients in the US and 4,000 to 5,000 in Europe. BridgeBio said it will charge insurers $75,446.58 for a 28-day supply, or just under $1 million a year. The approval gives patients with this subtype a treatment option for the first time. Source: STAT News.
